notes:
Wired gemini-3.7-flash into the fleet in the same shape as oxalpha (operator-verified headless 2026-08-25; canonical label `gemini-3.7-flash`, vendor serving tag `google/gemini-3.7-flash`, pi harness, openrouter backend). Six surfaces moved in step (T317 single source; T801 one canonicalizer, not four): (1) src/managent/main.zig canonical_models[] / serving_tag_map (added `google/gemini-3.7-flash` -> `gemini-3.7-flash`) / model_families[] (new vendor family `google`) / family_appetite[] (SPEND, equal-opportunity class per the 2026-08-24 operator ruling); (2) bin/dispatch MODELS / ALIASES / canonicalize_model; (3) bin/subagent PI_TAG_TO_CANONICAL / CANONICAL_TO_PI_TAG; (4) tools/fleet_caps.py FAMILY; (5) tools/run-record-model-backfill.py hard-coded canonicalizer (drift-checked against managent in arm E); (6) docs/infra/model-registry.md (canonical list, short-names table, serving-tags table, appetite table). Tools/model_tags.py and tools/model-profiles.py resolve the canonicalizer from managent (T801 seam) so they require no per-model edit.

Operator's short name `gflash` is an input alias ONLY — it lives in bin/dispatch ALIASES and the registry's short-names table, never in any source, doc, or binary as a stored label (arm H enforces this by grep). A `gemini-3.7-pro` near-miss is REFUSED at the boundary, not silently mapped (arm D2).

Acceptance verification (per the bundle's §Acceptance): (1) RED run captured before wiring — A and B failed; GREEN run after — all 12 arms pass. (2) Seeded-defect arm refuses gflashx (bin/dispatch), google/gemini-3.7-pro (managent canonicalize, exit 1), and gflash-as-stored-label (managent models does not list it). (3) `managent models` lists gemini-3.7-flash as the 12th label; `managent assign` draws it in the solo random pool (verified over 5 runs, 2 drew gemini-3.7-flash). (4) Dry-run dispatch resolves to `pi --model google/gemini-3.7-flash` both via the canonical label and via the `gflash` alias. (5) No source/doc/binary stores `gflash` outside bin/dispatch ALIASES and docs/infra/model-registry.md §Short names.

Findings (worth recording, even if not status changes):

(a) tools/run-record-model-backfill.py carries a hard-coded copy of the canonicalizer (lines 65-74) — a pre-T801 smudge. The T938 controls assert it stays in sync with managent (arm E5). The durable fix is to read from managent via tools/model_tags.py (T801 seam); the present sync guard is a stopgap. Note: a follow-up that migrates the backfill tool to the seam should retire the hard-coded list — claim this when the migration lands.

(b) The vendor family `google` is added but with no DEFAULT_FAMILY_CAP — openrouter has no recorded ceiling today, so it is uncapped (a cap can be set by the operator via FLEET_FAMILY_CAP=google=N when needed). The doc note lives in tools/fleet_caps.py FAMILY block.

(c) A new model surfaces in the model-perf.md table the next time a real gemini-3.7-flash lane dispatches; the T939 race arm is the first such lane and will land the perf entries. No claimlint C1a/C1b/C2/C6 regression — the four canonicalizer-parity and dispatch-regression suites stay green (regression-canonicalizer-parity.sh, regression-managent-models.sh, regression-dispatch.sh, regression-serving-tag-single-path.sh all ran PASS during this task).
